Fixing startup, sound and save problems

Most startup failures print their reason to a terminal. Start the game from a terminal first, then use the matching section below.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 5 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents
  1. Read the startup message
  2. Worlds that will not load
  3. Saving and losing progress
  4. Graphics driver problems
  5. Sound and music
  6. Record lag spikes for a bug report
  7. How this was checked

Read the startup message

When the game cannot start, or stops on a fatal error, it closes and prints a report that begins qiqi could not continue; its Error: (or Panic:) line gives the reason. The report is also saved as a details.txt file, and its last line, Diagnostic file:, says where. On Linux, a launch without options, such as from the application menu, also opens a qiqi could not continue window with Copy details and Close; it needs Python 3 and GTK 3. Windows and macOS show no window yet, so start the game from a terminal there to read the report.

  • A mistyped command-line option makes the game exit with code 2.
  • Any other failure makes it exit with code 1.

Messages you may see:

  • no Vulkan-compatible graphics adapter found: the graphics driver is missing. See Graphics driver problems below.
  • GPU ran out of memory during startup: lower Settings > Graphics > Display > Horizon distance, then try again.
  • Nearby terrain took too long to prepare; please try again: shown on the main menu. Try again, or lower Settings > Graphics > Display > Horizon distance.
  • audio disabled: playback command unavailable: sound players are missing. See Sound and music below.

Setup failures are written to an installer log. See Install, update and find your worlds.

Tip. Problems with other worlds appear on the main menu instead of closing the game.

Worlds that will not load

If a world cannot be read, the game shows World could not be loaded with the file and the reason, and keeps your save. Choose Back to menu to pick another world, or Open worlds folder to find the file. Keep its `.vxw` file, and copy it somewhere safe before trying repairs or a different game version.

Continue normally resumes the last selected local world. If that world will not open, use the error message to identify the affected file rather than assuming it is the default world.

See Saves and world files for loading limits and backups, and Install, update and find your worlds for the data folder.

Saving and losing progress

Press F6 to save a local world. If a save or stopped-host recovery fails, keep the game open and read the reported error before retrying or leaving.

For autosave, backups and the stopped-host recovery choices, follow Saves and world files. Opening Main menu while hosting does not stop the host.

Careful. A crash can lose unsaved progress. Keep a separate backup of a world you want to protect.

Graphics driver problems

Voxelgame needs a working Vulkan graphics driver. On Linux it runs in an X11 or XWayland session. It has no native Wayland window.

  • Debian and Fedora: the installer adds Mesa Vulkan drivers.
  • Arch: install vulkan-intel or vulkan-radeon, or your NVIDIA driver.
  • macOS: a Metal-capable GPU is required.

The game picks your high-performance GPU first. If that fails, it falls back to a software renderer such as llvmpipe. The fallback is useful for diagnosis but too slow for normal play.

To reduce GPU load, try Settings > Graphics > Display > Graphics preset > Low, or set Horizon distance lower, turn off Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics > Distant terrain, or set Shader to None (Graphics > Display).

Careful. Windows graphics have not been validated on a real Windows PC yet.

Sound and music

Sound effects need a player program: aplay from alsa-utils on Linux, or ffplay on Windows and macOS. The installers set these up. Without a player the game runs silently.

Music also needs ffmpeg to decode the songs. Song files may be mp3, ogg, wav or flac.

  • If ffmpeg is missing, Music turns itself off and the status line shows Music unavailable: ....
  • After you install ffmpeg, open Settings > Audio and switch Music back on.

Record lag spikes for a bug report

With the Performance overlay (F3) on, a frame that takes at least 25 ms and more than twice your frame budget is written to a log. Turn F3 off to stop recording. Lag-spike log

  • Linux: `~/.local/state/voxelgame/lag-spikes.jsonl`, or inside `$XDG_STATE_HOME/voxelgame` if that variable is set.
  • Each entry has the world seed, your position, the frame cost and up to eight of the slowest causes.
Tip. The F3 panel shows the log status: armed, recording, dropped or unavailable. Attach the file when you report a slow frame.

How this guide was checked

Error text, file paths, keys and save rules come from the game and installer source at the audited commit. Each ledger entry lists its source lines. The save and saving sections were narrowed against Voxelgame aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357 on 5 November 2026: src/worlds/resume.rs:12-40; src/app.rs:1043-1055,1553-1568,1641-1650,1904-1905; src/app/owner_recovery.rs:32-45. They link to the refreshed save/world guides instead of repeating older default-world or crafting-autosave assumptions. On 8 November 2026 the startup report, error window, unreadable-world dialog and Settings paths were re-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480: src/main.rs:33-50,93-109; src/fatal_error.rs:174-201,244-278,330-370; src/fatal_dialog.py:67-106; src/local_startup.rs:11-23; voxelgame-render startup_ui.rs:705-771; voxelgame-core settings.rs:25-89,653,933-989.

Initial ledger audit: Voxelgame main dd29d91, committed 10 October 2026; article updated 8 November 2026. Source-checked, not play-tested on every platform. Linux is the platform the installer is tested on. Windows and macOS graphics and sound are marked Limited because no real machine has validated them yet. These targeted save corrections are source checks only; no new play test was run. Other troubleshooting sections keep their earlier source checks.
